problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Euclidean Spaces (Orthogonal Bases)

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
examples.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the plane $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v}+t\mathbf{w},$ where $s,t\in\mathbb R,$ and
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068823/assets/11a1a4da746f8286edde9e12f17a7eaae9f4a242dfdab8ed137674c2d8e0c04c.png) 
Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the plane given that $\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{w}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3.$ 
And, since the set $\{\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by   

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} = \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\,\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{w}}\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{v}\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{13\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}v=\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{13\cdot 5+(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 3+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(21[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
